cards.q: What does a system design interviewer want to see?
cards.a: How you think: you agree on what to build first, break a big problem into small parts, know when to use each tool, and explain the tradeoffs.
What you gain and what you lose with a choice. Example: a cache makes reads faster, but the data can be a little old.

cards.q: What are the 6 steps of the interview framework?
cards.a: Requirements → Core Entities → API → Data Flow (optional) → High-Level Design → Deep Dives.

cards.q: How many features should you pick in the requirements step?
cards.a: About the top 3. Then say out loud what is out of scope, like user accounts or analytics. It shows you can focus.

cards.q: When is quick capacity math worth doing in an interview?
cards.a: Only when the answer changes your design. Example: 1 billion links × 500 bytes = 500 GB, which fits on one database, so no sharding just for size.

cards.q: What are the rules for the API step?
cards.a: One endpoint per feature. Use REST by default. Take the user ID from the login token, never from the request body.

cards.q: How should you build the high-level design?
cards.a: One feature at a time, with the simplest design that works. Leave caches, queues and sharding for the deep dives.

cards.q: How should you say a design choice out loud?
cards.a: Always with its tradeoff: "I chose X because..., the downside is...".
